edges.description: After mucosal invasion, S. Typhi can survive inside host macrophages in Salmonella-containing vacuoles.
Intestinal infection can progress to ulceration and perforation in severe late disease.
Vi expression supports macrophage survival by reducing antibacterial autophagy.
SPI-1 effectors activate caspase-1 and IL-1 beta responses in macrophages.
Intracellular survival supports systemic dissemination and culture-positive bacteremia.
Typhi expresses typhoid toxin within the Salmonella-containing vacuole.
Macrophage survival mechanisms enable dissemination to blood and reticuloendothelial sites.
SPI-1 inflammasome activation is one inflammatory arm of systemic bacteremic typhoid.
Culture-confirmed typhoid presents as a universal febrile syndrome in this cohort.
Gastrointestinal inflammatory disease commonly produces abdominal pain.
Systemic febrile illness commonly suppresses appetite.
Systemic febrile inflammation commonly produces headache.
Intestinal involvement can manifest with diarrhea.
Intestinal involvement can alternatively manifest with constipation.
Dissemination through the reticuloendothelial system enlarges the liver in a subset of cases.
Dissemination through the reticuloendothelial system enlarges the spleen in a subset of cases.
Necrotic ileal ulceration can perforate the bowel wall.
Fecal contamination of water or food brings viable S. Typhi to the small-intestinal epithelium.

evidence.snippet: S. Typhi expresses a range of virulence factors, including the virulence-associated (Vi) capsule, outer membrane proteins (OMPs), flagella, fimbriae, type III secretion systems (T3SSs) and other genes encoded on Salmonella pathogenicity islands (SPIs), as well as toxins, regulatory factors, and virulence plasmids.

nodes.description: S. Typhi SPI-1 effectors drive caspase-1 and IL-1 beta inflammasome activation in human monocyte-derived macrophages, providing a host-response link to bacteremic hyperinflammation.

evidence.reference_title: Hyperexpression of type III secretion system of Salmonella Typhi linked to a higher cytotoxic effect to monocyte-derived macrophages by activating inflammasome.
evidence.snippet: Thus, S. Typhi, relative to its non-typhoidal counterpart, S. Typhimurium, induces greater SPI-1-dependent inflammasome activation in monocyte-derived macrophages.

nodes.description: S. Typhi assembles a multipartite CdtB-PltA-PltB typhoid toxin and delivers the CdtB genotoxin from intracellular bacteria toward target cells.

evidence.reference_title: Delivery of a Salmonella Typhi exotoxin from a host intracellular compartment.
evidence.snippet: Here, we show that PltA and PltB, which are encoded in the same pathogenicity islet as cdtB, associate with CdtB to form a multipartite toxin.

evidence.reference_title: Delivery of a Salmonella Typhi exotoxin from a host intracellular compartment.
evidence.snippet: We also show that PltA and PltB are required for the delivery of CdtB from an intracellular compartment to target cells via autocrine and paracrine pathways.

nodes.description: The S. Typhi Vi capsule decreases macrophage macroautophagy through lower Nod2 and Galectin-8 expression, allowing greater intracellular bacterial survival than Vi-deficient mutants.

biological_processes: symbiont-mediated perturbation of host innate immune response

evidence.reference_title: Vi capsular polysaccharide of Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi disturbs autophagy to increase intracellular survival in macrophages.
evidence.snippet: In summary, we propose that Vi capsule of S. Typhi decreased autophagy of macrophages to increase its survival in host cells by decreasing the expression of Nod2 and Galectin-8.
